{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows negative sentiment (e.g., -0.25 or 0.00 with recent declines), as models tend to overestimate prices in bullish periods.",
    "Reduce forecast magnitude by 5-10% if the last 3-5 days show a sharp price drop (e.g., >10% decline) and sentiment is neutral or negative.",
    "Apply mean reversion correction: if forecast is >15% above recent 15-day average, reduce by 10-20% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.",
    "Avoid over-optimism after spikes: if model forecast exceeds true outcome by >20% in the first 5 days post-spike, reduce by 20-30% to prevent overcorrection.",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment: if sentiment > 0.5, allow 10-15% upward bias; if sentiment < -0.25, apply 10-15% downward bias.",
    "For long-term (30-day) forecasts, reduce volatility by smoothing with 3-day moving average of true outcomes to avoid overfitting to recent spikes.",
    "Correct for lag: if model forecast is significantly ahead of true outcome (e.g., >10% higher), reduce by 5-10% for the first 3 days, then adjust based on sentiment."
  ]
}
